reviewer: Codex, personal complete-final-answer read; no paid judge
primary_route: Continuous or early sampled product curves and substrate-titration kinetics.

checks.reason: No prospective no-enzyme/no-substrate background and known-response/procedural controls with their roles; changing enzyme or adding product does not define those controls.
No pre-execution consultation and transfer-check of prior Methods or validated protocols.
No detector reference calibration with acceptance limits and failed-calibration action; progress-curve shape is not a product-recovery calibration.
Rate units and a depletion bound are given, but no baseline-corrected measurement specification with weak/saturated/missing-signal rules.
No operational independent product/readout validation; repeated time points and enzyme titration retain the original detector artifact.

checks.quote: which confirms that the calculated 30 nmol/min rate is a valid initial velocity
checks.reason: Linear time-course signal is treated as confirming an artifact-free 30 nmol/min initial rate, and the valid interval is claimed to start strictly at time zero. A biased linear detector or pre-steady-state transient can defeat that decision.
Prescribes an inhibitor tight-binding formula for substrate sequestration without an inhibitor; explicit free-substrate/complex mass balance is needed instead.

checks.quote: A single lowered reaction rate proves that inhibition is occurring
checks.reason: A lower readout could result from less active enzyme or detector interference and does not prove molecular inhibition.
